page_title: Muster: never keep an agent waiting

summary.name: Muster
summary.one_liner: Muster is a free, open source macOS menu bar app that shows which Claude Code, Codex or Cursor session is waiting on you and lets you answer supported requests from an alert.
keywords: mac app to approve ai agent actions
use_cases: see which coding agent session needs input
approve or deny Claude Code commands from an alert
switch quickly between multiple agent sessions
track token usage and API-equivalent cost of sessions
monitor remote Claude Code sessions over SSH
summary.what_it_does: Muster runs in the macOS menu bar and counts sessions waiting on you from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. When a session needs input, an alert appears at the top of the screen; pressing ⌥↓ expands it to show the agent's reason, the full command, a file edit's size, or question options. Supported Claude Code and Codex requests can be allowed, denied or answered directly with shortcuts such as ⌥↩ or ⌥1 to ⌥3. Holding ⌥ and tapping Tab opens a switcher listing sessions from the last three hours, with the one waiting first, and each session shows tokens and API-list-price cost. It reads the session files agents already write and uses localhost for local hooks.
notable: Answer Claude Code and Codex requests directly from the alert with keyboard shortcuts
Holding ⌥ and tapping Tab switches between sessions, with the one waiting first
Raycast and Alfred integration via muster:// URLs
MIT licensed, no account, no app analytics
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; works on Apple silicon and Intel
Cursor prompts cannot be answered by Muster; it only shows the waiting chat and opens it
Direct answers work only for supported Claude Code and Codex requests after setup
SSH monitoring for remote hosts is described as coming in the upcoming 1.4
